selected_frontier: Test exactly one adjacent root-processed-write acknowledgment ambiguity with event1 and event2 already durable.
planned_atomic_boundary: Assume repository-visible root state transition processed=false->processed=true is atomic and is the complete durable representation of root processing for this exact probe. Crash occurs after attempting that write but before acknowledgment; post-crash durable state may be only processed=false or processed=true. On resume, event identity membership must prevent appending event1/event2 again; processed=false may transition once to true, processed=true must no-op.
tested_scope_guard: Exactly one two-event root, both event identities already durable exactly once, one atomic repository-visible processed boolean transition, one lost acknowledgment boundary. Excludes hidden side effects outside the durable root state, torn/corrupt writes, concurrent writers, identity collisions, nested frames, other event counts, hostile-size behavior and Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Execute the two allowed post-crash traces processed=false and processed=true under the frozen scope; verify neither resume path appends event1/event2 and both converge to processed=true without a second root-processing state transition when already true; persist result, update LATEST by CAS, create immutable own receipt, exact-read back, then return recurring-open.
